source_text: Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων πρὸς ταῦτα ἔφη· Εἶπον πρός σε, ὦ ἄνθρωπε, ὅτι ἀσφαλὴς ἐν πᾶσι σπουδάζεις εἶναι ταῖς γραφαῖς προσπλεκόμενος. Εἰπὲ δέ μοι. ἀληθῶς ὑμεῖς ἀνοικοδομηθῆναι τὸν τόπον Ἱερουσαλὴμ τοῦτον ὁμολογεῖτε, καὶ συναχθήσεσθαι τὸν λαὸν ὑμῶν καὶ εὐφρανθῆναι σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἅμα τοῖς πατριάρχαις καὶ τοῖς προφήταις καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῦ ἡμετέρου γένους ἢ καὶ τῶν προσηλύτων γενομένων πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ὑμῶν τὸν Χριστόν, προσδοκᾶτε, ἤ, ἵνα δόξῃς περικρατεῖν ἡμῶν ἐν ταῖς ζητήσεσι, πρὸς τὸ ταῦτα ὁμολογεῖν ἐχώρησας; Κἀγὼ εἶπον· Οὐχ οὕτω τάλας ἐγώ, ὦ Τρύφων, ὡς ἕτερα λέγειν παρ᾿ ἃ φρονῶ. Ὡμολόγησα οὖν σοι καὶ πρότερον ὅτι ἐγὼ μὲν καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοὶ ταῦτα φρονοῦμεν, ὡς καὶ πάντως ἐπίστασθαι τοῦτο γενησόμενον· πολλοὺς δ᾿ αὖ καὶ τῶν τῆς καθαρᾶς καὶ εὐσεβοῦς ὄντων Χριστιανῶν γνώμης τοῦτο μὴ γνωρίζειν ἐσήμανά σοι. Τοὺς γὰρ λεγομένους μὲν Χριστιανούς, ὄντας δὲ ἀθέους καὶ ἀσεβεῖς αἱρεσιώτας, ὅτι κατὰ πάντα βλάσφημα καὶ ἄθεα καὶ ἀνόητα διδάσκουσιν, ἐδήλωσά σοι. Ὅτι δ᾿ οὐκ ἐφ᾿ ὑμῶν μόνων τοῦτο λέγειν με ἐπίστασθε, τῶν γεγενημένων ἡμῖν λόγων ἁπάντων, ὡς δύναμίς μου, σύνταξιν ποιήσομαι, ἐν οἷς καὶ τοῦτο ὁμολογοῦντά με, ὃ καὶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁμολογῶ, ἐγγράψω. Οὐ γὰρ ἀνθρώποις μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρωπίνοις διδάγμασιν αἱροῦμαι ἀκολουθεῖν, ἀλλὰ θεῷ καὶ τοῖς παρ᾿ ἐκείνου διδάγμασιν. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ συνεβάλετε ὑμεῖς τισι λεγομένοις Χριστιανοῖς. καὶ τοῦτο μὴ ὁμολογοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ βλασφημεῖν τολμῶσι τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τὸν θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τὸν θεὸν Ἰακώβ. οἳ καὶ λέγουσι μὴ εἶναι νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν, ἀλλὰ ἅμα τῷ ἀποθνήσκειν τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ἀναλαμβάνεσθαι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, μὴ ὑπολάβητε αὐτοὺς Χριστιανούς, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ Ἰουδαίους, ἄν τις ὀρθῶς ἐξετάσῃ, ὁμολογήσειεν εἶναι τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους ἢ τὰς ὁμοίας αἱρέσεις Γενιστῶν καὶ Μεριστῶν καὶ Γαλιλαίων καὶ Ἑλληνιανῶν καὶ Φαρισαίων καὶ Βαπτιστῶν (καὶ μὴ ἀηδῶς ἀκούσητέ μου πάντα ἃ φρονῶ λέγοντος), ἀλλὰ λεγομένους μὲν Ἰουδαίους καὶ τέκνα Ἀβραάμ, καὶ χείλεσιν ὁμολογοῦντας τὸν θεόν, ὡς αὐτὸς κέκραγεν ὁ θεός, τὴν δὲ καρδίαν πόρρω ἔχειν ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ . Ἐγὼ δέ, καὶ εἴ τινές εἰσιν ὁρθογνώμονες κατὰ πάντα Χριστιανοί, καὶ σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν γενήσεσθαι ἐπιστάμεθα καὶ χίλια ἔτη ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ οἰκοδομηθείσῃ καὶ κοσμηθείσῃ καὶ πλατυνθείσῃ. ὡς οἱ προφῆται Ἰεζεκιὴλ καὶ Ήσαΐας [voy. ch. suivant] καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι ὁμολογοῦσιν.
pass_a_gloss: And Trypho said to these things, I told you, O man, that you strive to be safe in all the scriptures being entwined. But tell me, do you truly confess that this place Jerusalem will be rebuilt, and your people will be gathered and will rejoice with the Christ, together with the patriarchs and the prophets and the saints of our race, or even of the proselytes who became such before your Christ came, do you expect this, or did you yield to confess these things so that you might seem to overcome us in the investigations? And I said, I am not so foolish, O Trypho, as to say other things than what I think. So I confessed to you also before that I and many others think these things, as we certainly know that this will happen; but I also indicated to you that many of the pure and pious Christians do not know this. For those who are called Christians, but are atheists and impious heretics, I showed you that they teach blasphemous and atheistic and foolish things. That I do not say these things only about you, you know from all the words that have happened between us, as far as my power, I will make a composition, in which I will also write, confessing these things, which I also confess to you. For I do not choose to follow human teachings more than divine teachings, but God and the teachings from Him. For even if you have met some so-called Christians who do not confess these things, but even dare to blaspheme God, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, who also say that there is no resurrection of the dead, but that their souls are taken up into heaven as soon as they die, do not suppose them to be Christians, just as, if someone examines correctly, they would not confess the Sadducees or similar sects of Genistae and Meristae and Galilaeans and Hellenians and Pharisees and Baptists (and do not be annoyed at hearing all that I think and say), but so-called Jews and children of Abraham, and with their lips confessing God, as God Himself has cried out, but having their heart far from Him. But I, even if there are some orthodox Christians in all respects, and we know that there will be a resurrection of the flesh, and Jerusalem will be built and adorned and enlarged for a thousand years, as the prophets Ezekiel and Isaiah and the others confess.
pass_b_english: Trypho responded, "I told you, my friend, that you strive to make your position secure in every way by intertwining yourself with the Scriptures. But tell me this: do you truly confess that this place Jerusalem will be rebuilt, and that your people will be gathered and will rejoice with the Christ, together with the patriarchs, the prophets, and the saints of our race—or even those proselytes who converted before your Christ came? Do you expect this, or did you only agree to confess these things so that you might appear to overcome us in these debates?" I answered, "I am not so foolish, Trypho, as to say things other than what I actually think. I have already confessed to you that I and many others hold this view, fully convinced that it will certainly happen. Yet I also made it clear to you that many who are pure and pious Christians do not share this knowledge. I pointed out to you that those who are called Christians but are actually atheists and impious heretics teach things that are blasphemous, godless, and senseless."

"You know from all the words that have passed between us, as far as my ability allows, that I am not saying these things only about you. I will compile an account in which I will also write, confessing these very things that I now confess to you. For I choose to follow not human teachings more than divine ones, but God and the teachings that come from Him. Even if you have encountered some so-called Christians who do not confess these things, but even dare to blaspheme the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—who also say there is no resurrection of the dead, but that their souls are taken up into heaven the moment they die—do not suppose them to be Christians. Just as, if someone examines the matter correctly, they would not acknowledge the Sadducees or similar sects of Genistae, Meristae, Galilaeans, Hellenians, Pharisees, and Baptists to be true Jews—(please do not be annoyed at hearing all that I think and say)—but only so-called Jews and children of Abraham who confess God with their lips, as God Himself has cried out, yet have their hearts far from Him."

"But as for me, and any who are orthodox Christians in every respect, we know that there will be a resurrection of the flesh, and that Jerusalem will be built, adorned, and enlarged for a thousand years, just as the prophets Ezekiel and Isaiah and the others confess." (Ezekiel; Isaiah)

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains all theological distinctions (e.g., the distinction between 'so-called Jews' and 'true Jews' implied by the comparison to the sects). Scripture citations for Ezekiel and Isaiah are correctly added as per instructions.
